entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 Date of Institution : 13.01.2014 Reserved for Judgment : 23.09.2025 Date of Decision : 07.11.2025 JUDGMENT 1.

Briefly stated the case of the prosecution is that the complainant, who was a foreign national, has come to India along with his wife and on the intervening night of 05.01.2012 and 06.01.2012, they hired a prepaid taxi bearing No. DL IT 6894 for Paharganj for going to their hotel which was already booked.
That the taxi driver informed the complainant that he was not able to find the hotel and thus, the complainant had given him mobile number of the hotel.
That the taxi driver called the hotel and he informed the complainant that he was informed by the hotel that there was no room available in the hotel as due to fog many trains were cancelled.
That thereafter, the driver told the complainant that he knew a person and took the complainant and his wife to a travel agent.
That the travel agent reiterated the same story about hotels rooms being not available.
That the said agent started offering tour packages to the complainant despite their resistance.
That the the said travel agent prepared a Rajasthan tour for the complainant and also started threatening the complainant and his wife.
The complainant alleged that the said agent took the visa card of the complainant, took his signatures forcibly and had withdrawn Rs. 1,16,500/- and called a taxi for the complainant and his wife.
The complainant and his wife then left for Puskhar and ultimately sought help from German Embassy.
The complainant and his wife reported the matter at PS IGI Airport and then the present FIR was registered.
During the course of investigation, the travel agent was identified as accused Jahangir Ahmed Wani and the taxi driver was identified as accused Rajender.

After completion of the investigation, the charge-sheet was filed under section 420/384/120B IPC and section 4 Delhi Prevention of Touting and Malpractices Against Tourist Act (herein after referred to as 'DPTMT Act')
2.

entities.text: Delhi Prevention of Touting and Malpractices Against Tourist Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Vide order dated 24.05.2014, cognizance of the offence was taken and the accused was summoned.

After compliance with section 207 Cr.P.C, vide order dated 17.01.2017, charges for the offences under section 384 read with section 120B IPC and section 4(a) DPTMT Act were framed upon the accused, to which they accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
Thereafter, the case was fixed for prosecution evidence.

3. During the trial of the case, the prosecution was unable to secure presence of the complainant Sh.
Kai Trostrum and his wife Ms. Shirin, despite repeated summons being issued, including summons through MHA.
Vide order dated 22.07.2019, PW Kai Trostrum was dropped as witness.

Similarly,
Ms. Shirin was also dropped from the list of witness on 11.07.2025 as she remained unserved.
There were no other eye witness or public witness who can prove the charge against the accused persons.
The remaining witness were either police or formal witnesses.
No purpose would have been served by completing the formality of trial without there being any hope for the prosecution to secure conviction of the accused in the present case.

It was held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Satish Mehra Vs. Delhi Administration, 1996 9 SCC 766, that when the Judge is fairly certain that there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction the valuable time of the Court should not be wasted for holding a trial only for the purpose of formally completing the procedure to pronounce the State vs Jahangir Ahmed Wani Etc on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31844231/
2 conclusion on a future date.

sentences.text:
Since, nothing incriminating had come on record against the accused,
his statement under section 313 Cr.P.C was also dispensed with.

4. In view of the fact that testimony of the complainant Kai Trostrum ans Ms. Shirin could not be secured to prove the allegations made against the accused persons and in the absence of any other independent witness to prove the same, the case of the prosecution against the accused must fail.
Accordingly, the accused Jahangir Ahmed Wani and Rajender Singh are acquitted of the charges under section 384 read with section 120B IPC and section 4(a) DPTMT Act.
